_comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later — PR review molecule template. Instantiate with scripts/bd/new-pr-review-molecule.sh <PR-NUMBER>. Every {{PR}} is substituted with the PR number.

nodes.title: Review PR #{{PR}} (contributor PR review molecule)
nodes.description:
End-to-end review of an external contributor PR on agentic-forges/forgejo-mcp, from triage to hardening.

Run the children in dependency order; each names the skill, agent, or castra command that does the work. Three standing rules apply throughout:

1. DETERMINISM (CLAUDE.md): if a step can be a shell script or a git hook, make it one. Do not leave a recurring check to an agent's attention.
2. The contributor is a guest. Diagnose before asking. Never hand someone an error message they could have read themselves — hand them the cause and the fix.
3. CASTRA IS THE FORGE-SIDE ARM (castra v0.3.0, .castra/ in this repo, 'castra --help'). It is forge-agnostic and already knows this repo's conventions: use it for the per-issue bot-active mutex, isolated persona worktrees, run-status comments, and the label vocabulary. An interactive session and the castra bot can both be holding this PR — coordinate through the mutex rather than racing.

Source: distilled from the review of PR #481 (feat(attachments): accept local file paths) on 2026-08-13.

nodes.title: PR #{{PR}}: triage and classify
nodes.description:
Take the PR, then give it its Kind/* and Priority/* labels.

CASTRA FIRST — claim the PR before touching it:
  castra label ...          # acquire the per-issue bot-active mutex (castra:bot-active). See 'castra label --help'; releasing it is the closeout step.
  castra issue view <PR-URL>
  castra pr review-threads <PR-URL>   # inline review comments the MCP issue-comment list does NOT show
Skipping review-threads is how you end up repeating a point a human already made inline.

Optionally hand the whole read to the packaged persona instead of doing it by hand — it is read-only, holds no write credential, and returns a structured verdict (one of insufficient|sufficient|blocked|duplicate) with clarity scores and candidate labels:
  castra persona-run --persona triage --input issue_url=<PR-URL> --output-dir <dir>
  castra persona-validate <result-file>
  castra persona-run --persona triage --dry-run   # renders the prompt only

SKILL: codeberg-issue-triage (the triage heuristics carry over to this forge).

TOOLS (b4mad MCP, never the web UI):
  mcp__b4mad__get_pull_request_by_index owner=agentic-forges repo=forgejo-mcp index={{PR}}
  mcp__b4mad__list_repo_labels  owner=agentic-forges repo=forgejo-mcp    # or: castra label --repo agentic-forges/forgejo-mcp
  mcp__b4mad__add_issue_labels  owner=agentic-forges repo=forgejo-mcp index={{PR}} labels=<numeric ids, comma separated>

Label ids are NOT stable across forges — always list them first, never reuse ids from CLAUDE.md's Codeberg table.

Judgement, not reflex: Kind/Security means 'this PR fixes a vulnerability', not 'this PR touches a sensitive surface'. If the change opens a new capability worth scrutiny (arbitrary host file reads, token handling, command execution), say so in prose to the human instead of mislabelling.

DONE: Kind/* and Priority/* set; any security-relevant surface flagged to the human in the session summary.

nodes.title: PR #{{PR}}: reproduce every red CI check locally
nodes.description:
Never review a red PR from the check name alone. Get the real error.

STEP 1 — find the run. Tekton TaskRuns get pruned within hours, so logs are usually already gone:
  oc get pipelinerun -A | grep <pipelinerun-name>
  tkn -n <ns> pipelinerun logs <name>      # try first; expect 'not found'

STEP 2 — when logs are gone, recover the command from the embedded spec. This always works, because the PipelineRun stores the resolved taskSpec:
  oc -n <ns> get pipelinerun <name> -o json | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(json.dumps([t for t in d['status']['pipelineSpec']['tasks'] if t['name']=='<task>'][0], indent=1))"
Read .steps[].script — that is the exact command to run locally, and .spec.params.revision is the commit it ran against.

STEP 3 — reproduce at the PR head in an isolated worktree (never in the user's working tree). Prefer castra, which names the branch and directory consistently:
  castra prepare-run --persona review --issue {{PR}} --base <revision-from-step-2>
Or by hand:
  git fetch upstream refs/pull/{{PR}}/head:refs/remotes/upstream/pr-{{PR}}
  git worktree add <scratchpad>/pr{{PR}} refs/remotes/upstream/pr-{{PR}} --detach
Then run each step's script in that worktree. Note that a later 'git pull --rebase' prunes the pr-{{PR}} remote ref and leaves the worktree detached — harmless, but do not be surprised.

AGENT: delegate to Explore if locating the pipeline/task definitions means sweeping .tekton/ — keep the log dumps out of the main context.

DONE: the failure reproduced locally, with the exact error text captured verbatim for the comment.

nodes.title: PR #{{PR}}: find the root cause and verify the fix before writing a word
nodes.description:
Reproducing is not diagnosing. Find WHY, then PROVE the fix.

Method that worked on #481: compare the failing artifact against a passing sibling in the same repo. The validator message ('must contain SHALL or MUST') was misleading — SHALL was plainly present on line two. Diffing against a passing delta showed the passing ones were unwrapped single lines, which located the real rule: only the first physical line is inspected.

Then APPLY the candidate fix in the throwaway worktree and re-run the CI command. Do not post a fix you have not seen turn the check green. Report the resulting totals ('24 passed, 0 failed') in the comment — it is what makes the ask credible.

Also run the steps AFTER the failing one. A step-1 failure means steps 2+ never ran and may hide further breakage.

DONE: root cause stated in one sentence; fix verified green locally; any downstream steps confirmed.

nodes.title: PR #{{PR}}: post the diagnosis and the fix to the author
nodes.description:
One comment: what is red, the verbatim error, WHY it is red, the exact fix, and evidence you verified it. Then ask politely.

TOOL: mcp__b4mad__create_issue_comment owner=agentic-forges repo=forgejo-mcp index={{PR}} body=...

Structure that worked:
  1. Thank them and name the real problem their PR solves (shows you read it).
  2. 'Heads-up that <pipeline> is red (PipelineRun <name>, revision <sha>). I reproduced it locally with <command>; it is a small formatting nit, not a design problem.'
  3. Fenced block with the actual validator output.
  4. **Cause:** with the specific lines, and — where possible — why a sibling part of their own PR passes. Contrast teaches faster than a rule.
  5. **Fix:** a copy-pasteable corrected block, plus which repo convention it matches.
  6. 'I verified this makes the whole suite green.'
  7. A concrete, polite ask.

Tone: the author does not know this repo's conventions. That is the repo's failure to document, not theirs.

CASTRA: for run-scoped progress (as opposed to the human-readable review), use 'castra status --persona review --run-id <id>' — it posts and then UPDATES one per-run comment instead of stacking new ones. Use it for pipeline noise; use a real comment for anything the author must read.

DONE: comment posted; permalink recorded for the human.

nodes.title: PR #{{PR}}: request a Showboat demo, with an unconditional offer to do it instead
PR #{{PR}}: delegate follow-up discovery to a subagent and file beads
PR #{{PR}}: turn the CI failure into a deterministic local guard
nodes.description:
The point of the review is that the NEXT contributor does not hit this. CLAUDE.md: if it can be a script or a git hook, it must be.

Pattern used for #481 (three layers, each doing only what it can):
  1. .editorconfig — stop editors REINTRODUCING the problem (it cannot enforce anything; be honest about that).
  2. scripts/ci/<check>.sh — a POSIX sh wrapper that SHELLS OUT to the same tool CI runs rather than re-implementing its rules. One source of truth, and every rule is covered, not just the one that bit us. Skip with a warning when the tool is absent so contributors are not blocked. On failure, print a targeted hint when the upstream error message is misleading.
  3. .pre-commit-config.yaml — wire the script in, scoped with 'files:' to the paths that matter.
  4. DEVELOPER.md — document the convention and how to run the gate locally.

CASTRA ALTERNATIVE — do not do this inline if it is a well-scoped chunk someone else can own. File the guard as its own issue and put the 'code' trigger label on it: that hands it to the castra code bot, which implements, pushes a branch, and opens a PR. Escalate with 'castra:human' if it stalls or needs a judgement call. Inline is right when the fix is small and you already have the failing tree in front of you (as with #481); delegation is right when it is a separable chunk of work.

If a persona produced the branch, publish it with 'castra post-run' rather than pushing by hand.

VERIFY ALL THREE PATHS before committing: exit 0 clean, exit 1 with hint on a known-bad tree (reuse the PR worktree), exit 0 with warning when the tool is off PATH. Then 'pre-commit run <hook> --all-files'.

DONE: guard committed; all three exit paths demonstrated.

nodes.title: PR #{{PR}}: commit and push the guard
nodes.description:
SKILL: ds:commit — always. Never hand-craft the git commit command (CLAUDE.md).

Conventional commit; emoji goes AFTER the first colon ('chore: 🔧 ...'). Body explains why the failure was confusing, not just what changed. Footer: 'Assisted-by: <Model> via <Tool>'.

The repo default branch is main and 'origin' is a personal fork while 'upstream' is agentic-forges — check 'git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{u}' before pushing so the commit lands where you think it does.

Branch first unless the human explicitly says to commit to main.

DONE: 'git status -sb' shows the branch in sync with its upstream.

nodes.title: PR #{{PR}}: set review-state labels
nodes.description:
Once the review is delivered and the ball is in the author's court, label the STATE so the next person sees it without reading ten comments.

  Reviewed/Confirmed      — a human/agent has reviewed it
  Status/Need More Info   — waiting on the author to act
  Status/Blocked          — blocked on something EXTERNAL; do not use it for 'waiting on author', that double-signals

mcp__b4mad__add_issue_labels adds without replacing, so earlier Kind/* and Priority/* labels survive.

If the vocabulary does not fit (this repo has no Reviewed/Changes-Requested, and Reviewed/Confirmed reads as 'bug reproduced'), use the closest label AND tell the human the vocabulary is the problem. Do not silently misuse a label.

CASTRA: the vocabulary is meant to be declarative, not hand-curated —
  castra init-labels --repo agentic-forges/forgejo-mcp --file <labels.json> --dry-run
is idempotent and shows the plan before touching the forge. NOTE (verified 2026-08-13): this repo's .castra/ holds only personas/ and prompts/ — there is no labels.json here yet, so fixing a vocabulary gap properly means adding one (the lage repo has a working example). Until then, report the gap rather than inventing labels by hand.

DONE: state labels set; any vocabulary gap reported.

nodes.title: PR #{{PR}}: close out the session
nodes.description:
SKILL: done-with.

CLAUDE.md session-completion protocol — work is NOT complete until push succeeds:
  git pull --rebase
  bd dolt push          # beads created during review are otherwise stranded locally
  git push
  git status            # MUST show up to date with origin

CASTRA: RELEASE THE MUTEX you acquired in the triage step ('castra label ...' — see its --help). A stuck castra:bot-active label makes the bot skip this PR forever, and nobody will notice quickly. If you are leaving the PR needing a human decision rather than author action, set 'castra:human' as well. Close the run with 'castra status --persona review --status success|failure --run-id <id>' so the per-run comment does not sit unresolved.

Then: close finished beads, remove throwaway git worktrees ('git worktree list' — the PR worktree from the reproduce step), and hand off with the PR permalinks, the bead ids filed, and exactly what the contributor was asked for.

DONE: everything pushed; mutex released; scratch worktrees gone; handoff written.
